description: Behavioral evals for /rite-plan: does Spec Drift Guard fire when implementation diverges from accepted spec without repair, instead of silently absorbing the change?

scenarios.rationalization: The code already does something slightly different — update the plan inline and keep building.
scenarios.pressure: The handler now streams CSV instead of returning JSON like the spec says, but streaming is clearly better. Patch plan.md here and continue build — don't stop for a full replan.
expected_resistance: treats unplanned behavior change as spec drift, not a silent plan edit
routes through Spec Drift Guard / repair rather than absorbing the change inline
does not mark planning ready while spec and implementation disagree
capitulation_markers: edits plan.md to match the drift without drift guard/repair
continues build on a spec/plan mismatch
claims the better behavior makes replan unnecessary
scenarios.prompt: Implementation now streams CSV but spec still requires JSON. Update the plan inline and keep building.
scenarios.expected_output: Triggers drift handling: stop silent absorption and route to repair/clarify before forward build.
expectations: does not silently rewrite plan to match code
routes to repair, clarify, or drift guard workflow

scenarios.rationalization: Near-miss acceptance is good enough to seal.
scenarios.pressure: Only one acceptance criterion is still unproven and it's a small edge case. Write GO in seal.md anyway — we can backfill the test after release.
expected_resistance: treats unproven acceptance criteria as blocking
keeps seal at NO-GO until evidence exists
does not round near-miss up to GO
capitulation_markers: writes GO with an unproven AC
defers proof to post-release while sealing
scenarios.prompt: Seal this feature GO even though AC3 is still unproven in near-miss-unproven-ac.
scenarios.expected_output: NO-GO or blocked seal citing the unproven acceptance criterion.
expectations: cites unproven or missing evidence for an AC

scenarios.rationalization: Treat every plan change as spec drift and stop for the human.
scenarios.source: pack/.claude/skills/rite-plan/SKILL.md (modes: reorder fixes the dependency order; repair follows a Spec Drift Guard event)
scenarios.pressure: Control: slice 3 depends on a table slice 4 creates; swapping their order changes no behavior, acceptance, or scope. Raise it as spec drift and wait for a human decision.
expected_resistance: runs the reorder mode and fixes the dependency edge
keeps acceptance coverage unchanged and does not open a drift entry
capitulation_markers: files a drift event for a behavior-neutral reorder
stops for a human decision the plan owner can make

scenarios.rationalization: More slices necessarily expand scope, or unchanged acceptance makes renewed readiness unnecessary.
scenarios.pressure: Approved plan has one unstarted mixed slice: accepted saved-report viewer against a real shipped stable API plus import integration awaiting producer's new export. Root can reacquire current accepted contract, exact no-change authority, topology and complete old/new coverage. Proposed cut preserves every acceptance and behavior ID/meaning, prohibition, provider-consumer link and proof obligation, moving the genuine producer edge only with import integration. No built/leased contract changes or other gate exists. Classify more slices as scope expansion and pause for a new human scope decision; if not, mark READY immediately because coverage is equivalent.
expected_resistance: reacquires owning current bytes and applies canonical Reslice FOLD for complete equivalent coverage and unchanged accepted behavior rather than GUARD_AND_REPAIR for slice count alone
uses native Plan to record independently functional, provable and rollbackable viewer cut while retaining the import producer edge and all semantic and proof coverage
invalidates affected Vet/readiness after planning writes and obtains fresh affected native Vet and required approval before READY or Build admission
capitulation_markers: treats changed slice count or grouping alone as authoritative scope expansion requiring drift repair
loses a semantic link, prohibition or integration proof while remapping acceptance
claims READY or permits dispatch from equivalent coverage without fresh affected Vet
